clue.text: End of a raft, riddled from stem to stern

indicators.note: riddled suggests something shot through and broken up, so the preceding words are jumbled

explanation.surface: The tail of a raft is shot full of holes along its whole length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riddled' makes an anagram of the ten letters of ENDOFARAFT.
explanation.definitionFit: Lengthwise along a ship, from bow to rear, is the nautical meaning of the phrase.

clue.text: Examination of French internal trial

indicators.note: internal puts the French word inside the exam

parts.note: an oral is a spoken exam
de is French for of

explanation.surface: A test of the French language within an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: A painful test of endurance, a synonym for a severe trial.

clue.text: I'm sorry for the dance

explanation.surface: An apology for a ballroom dance.
explanation.walkthrough: An excuse-me is a dance where partners may be cut in on.
explanation.definitionFit: A polite apology phrase also names a dance in which one may cut in on another couple.

clue.text: Fairly good cleaner

explanation.surface: A reasonably good cleaning lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not so dusty' is a British idiom for not bad; read literally it means less dusty.
explanation.definitionFit: The colloquial phrase means not bad at all; literally it describes something with less dirt.

clue.text: A don listened to a dissertation

indicators.note: listened to signals that the words are to be heard rather than read

parts.note: to don is to dress, put clothes on, so a don gives a dress

explanation.surface: A university lecturer heard a lengthy scholarly piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'don' looks like the lecturer, but it is the verb meaning put on.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal speech or discourse is a kind of dissertation.

clue.text: Stood up a second girl

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: set means stood, placed upright

explanation.surface: A second girl was jilted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stood up' looks like jilted, but 'up' turns SET into TES.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, as in Hardy's heroine, stands for a girl.

clue.text: Becoming breathless? Start off 80x 24÷51

annotationWithheld.why: Becoming breathless? Start off 80x 24÷51 (8), as the scan prints it: no parse of the numbers gives EXHALING and no source explains them.

clue.text: Old lady with bird crossing reef the wrong way causes this

definitions.text: crossing reef the wrong way causes this

parts.note: granny is an affectionate word for an old woman
the knot is a wading bird

explanation.surface: A grandmother and a bird tangle a reef the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: A reef knot crossed the wrong way slips; 'reef' looks like the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The insecure tie results from crossing the ends of a reef knot incorrectly.

clue.text: Team overwhelmed by anger restored by panacea

indicators.note: a team overwhelmed by something sits swamped inside it
restored is read as re-stored, put back, so the anger word is turned round

parts.note: to rile is to anger
XI, eleven, is a cricket or football team

explanation.surface: A side beaten by fury is revived by a cure-all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restored', read as stored back, is the turning signal; 'overwhelmed by' means the team is swamped inside the angry word.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are supposed universal remedies; an elixir is an alchemist's cure for all ills.

clue.text: Taught eastern pressman about money once

indicators.note: the eastern pressman goes about, that is around, the old coin

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is a newspaperman
a ducat was a gold coin formerly used in Europe

explanation.surface: An oriental journalist taught about old coinage.
explanation.walkthrough: E and ED together make EED, and the coin sits after the first E.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has been taught has been schooled, so the past participles match.

clue.text: Soldiers make an effort to keep down

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
to strain is to make an effort

explanation.surface: Troops try hard to hold something back.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold in check or suppress is a synonym.

clue.text: Butterfly stroke, perhaps

explanation.surface: A swimming stroke named after an insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butterfly stroke' looks like swimming. Stroke is the oarsman nearest the stern; a Blue is someone who has represented Oxford or Cambridge, as in the Boat Race.
explanation.definitionFit: A blue is a small butterfly; an Oxbridge rower such as the stroke may win a sporting colour of that name.

clue.text: Reveal the secret of a love-child, giving all the details

parts.note: to blow a secret is to give it away
a by-blow is an old word for an illegitimate child

explanation.surface: Exposing a scandal about an illegitimate child in full detail.
explanation.definitionFit: A minutely detailed account, as of a fight's every punch, is described with this phrase.

clue.text: I sit badly-I got beaten in the handicap

indicators.note: beaten, like eggs, means whisked up, so the words before it are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sat awkwardly and got thrashed in a race with weights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' belongs to the fodder; 'got' and 'in the' are links, and 'beaten' shuffles ISITBADLYI.
explanation.definitionFit: A disadvantage or impairment is a synonym for a handicap.

clue.text: Ark not entirely amicably arranged for the transport of captives

indicators.note: arranged means the letters are put in a new order
not entirely means the last letter of the word is dropped

explanation.surface: A boat assembled somewhat amicably to carry prisoners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' drops the Y of amicably; ARK plus AMICABL are then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A police van for carrying prisoners is the slang name.

clue.text: Separate headlines following outside broadcast

annotationWithheld.why: Separate headlines following outside broadcast (7): the definition 'head' (obverse side of a coin) and the wordplay 'lines' (VERSE) both come from the one word 'headlines', split by 'Separate'; one word doing two jobs.

clue.text: American left nurse holding the animal

indicators.note: the nurse holds, contains, the animal

parts.note: a VAD was a volunteer nurse of the Voluntary Aid Detachment
a moose is the large North American deer

explanation.surface: A US soldier abandoned a nurse who was keeping a pet.
explanation.walkthrough: VAD is a British wartime volunteer nursing service.
explanation.definitionFit: This is US slang meaning departed hurriedly.

clue.text: Nonpareil is a size of type

explanation.surface: A peerless one is also a printer's measure.
explanation.walkthrough: Nonpareil is itself also a size of type, which tempts one to read the clue as a single definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A model of excellence is unequalled; in old printing, a named type size of about twenty points shares the word.

clue.text: By the sound of it, leant forward

definitions.text: By the sound of it, leant

explanation.surface: Apparently someone bent forwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leant forward' reads as one phrase; split it: 'leant' heard is lent, as money is lent, meaning advanced, and 'forward' is a second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Forward and advanced both describe being ahead or progressive.

clue.text: Measure hair that's not been cut

parts.note: fur is animal hair
uncut hair stays long

explanation.surface: Gauge the hair that hasn't been trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of length, an eighth of a mile, used in horse racing.

clue.text: City has nothing but dried fish

parts.note: Bombay, now Mumbai, is an Indian city
in cricket a duck is a score of nothing

explanation.surface: A town offers only salted fish.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a South Asian fish, the bummalo, eaten dried and salted.

clue.text: Huge container — about the ultimate in hugeness

indicators.note: the container goes about, around, the letter picked

parts.note: a vat is a large tank

indicators.note: the ultimate in a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: An enormous tank holds the very peak of bigness.
explanation.definitionFit: Immense or enormous, a plain synonym.

clue.text: One recording the points raised about fabulous birds

indicators.note: raised in a down entry means the pieces are read upwards

parts.note: re means about, concerning
rocs are giant birds of Arabian legend

explanation.surface: A tallier lifted about some legendary birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns RE plus ROCS as a whole, giving SCOR and ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who keeps the tally in a game records the points.

clue.text: Guider gets worn out in the amphitheatre

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the arena

parts.note: a bowl is an open-air stadium shaped like a basin, such as the Hollywood Bowl

indicators.note: worn out means broken down, so the letters of worn are reworked

explanation.surface: A guide leader is exhausted in the arena.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worn out' looks like tired, but 'out' is an anagram signal; Guiders are adult leaders in the Girl Guides, and a Brownie pack's leader has this title.
explanation.definitionFit: The adult leader of a Brownie pack in the Guide movement bears this title; Guiders are its adult leaders.

clue.text: On a testament, hand primarily signifies this

definitions.text: On a testament, hand primarily signifies this

indicators.note: primarily means take the first letter of each of these words

explanation.surface: A hand placed on a Bible signals a sworn promise.
explanation.definitionFit: A solemn promise is sworn with a hand on a holy book.

clue.text: Label is known to the public

explanation.surface: A tag is publicly known.
explanation.walkthrough: A label is printed on a gramophone disc, so it is literally found there.
explanation.definitionFit: A label sits on a disc; a statement made openly and officially documented is publicly stated.

clue.text: Some lettuce (only a bit of the heart) used in dish

indicators.text: only a bit of the heart
indicators.note: only a bit of the heart means a short run from inside the words, the core of the phrase

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A salad leaf, just a scrap of its centre, goes into a recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'the heart) used in dish' as the definition; the bracket is the hidden-word signal and 'dish' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A food made of beaten eggs cooked in a pan is a dish.

clue.text: Stranded dinghy hard to get moving

indicators.note: getting the letters moving shuffles them into a new order

explanation.surface: A small boat beached and difficult to refloat.
explanation.definitionFit: Left aground or stuck without help, a common idiom.
